master.text: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password changes are checked against a set of breached passwords.

predecessors.text: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration, login, and password change are checked against a set of breached passwords either locally (such as the top 1,000 or 10,000 most common passwords which match the system's password policy) or using an external API. If using an API a zero knowledge proof or other mechanism should be used to ensure that the plain text password is not sent or used in verifying the breach status of the password. If the password is breached, the application must require the user to set a new non-breached password. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

summaries.body:
V6.2.12 is ADDED, SPLIT FROM v4.0.3-2.1.7. That predecessor required passwords submitted at registration, login, and password change to be checked against a breached-password set, locally (top 1,000 or 10,000 common passwords matching policy) or via an API using a zero-knowledge proof so the plaintext was not sent, and to force a new non-breached password on hit.

On 16 November 2018 Michael Burnett (#308) argued the then-"verifier compromise resistance" 2.1.7 duplicated V2.5; vanderaj agreed two days later (9ace43e4). The remaining 4.0 control is the breach-check text from which 5.0 split V6.2.12 (breach set) and V6.2.4 (common-password list).

vanderaj added a zero-knowledge-proof sentence to V2.1.7 on 20 February 2019 (14f211ae). A 21 February reword closed #491 (9656238e). On 25 February tghosth "softened the breached passwords requirement" (df20c0e6).

The 5.0 split dropped login-time checking, the local-vs-API / ZKP mechanics, and the explicit "require a new non-breached password" sentence from this ID. V6.2.12 is only: registration or password-change submissions are checked against a set of breached passwords. The common-password numeric list and policy-matching language moved to V6.2.4.
